core_obligations: Identify the support of a sheaf of rings A on S_etale with the support of the unit section of A (proof lines 4062-4065): the stalk of A vanishes at a point exactly when the germ of the unit section is zero there.
Invoke the chapter's own convention for the zero ring (proof lines 4062-4064): a ring is 0 if and only if 1 = 0, which is what turns vanishing of the ring stalk into vanishing of the unit germ.
Conclude that the support of the sheaf of rings is the support of the unit section, hence closed (proof line 4065 against the assertion at source line 4058).
proof_roadmap: Read the statement: for a sheaf of rings on S_etale the set of points where the stalk is nonzero is closed.
Apply the chapter convention that a ring is zero if and only if 1 = 0.
Hence the support of the sheaf of rings equals the support of the unit section.
The support of a section is closed, so the required set is closed.
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts closedness of the support of a sheaf of rings on the small etale site S_etale (statement lines 4056-4059). The only operation is the reduction of the vanishing of a ring stalk to the vanishing of the germ of the unit section, carried out through the chapter's own convention that a ring is 0 if and only if 1 = 0 (proof lines 4062-4064). Nothing beyond that convention and the definition of support is used, and the closing step is the standard closedness of the support of a section. The claim is H2: one explicit identification, very short verification.
